summary: Presque Isle Harbor Breakwater Light, Marquette, Lake Superior: a 1941 light at the end of a breakwater extended in the 1930s, automated by the 1970s.

light.fog_signal: electric horn (the original air diaphone was removed)

lens.note: Modern LED marine beacon; the original optic was replaced (NRHP p. 8-9).

structures.note: About 55 ft (16.8 m) from water to top of tower; the steel tower alone is about 30 ft (9 m). Record gives 12.0 m.
Rectangular concrete pier with an octagonal concrete first story.

access.note: Reached on foot along the breakwater; the light is not open to visitors (NRHP p. 4). The breakwater is dangerous in high waves (memorial sign, LighthouseFriends).

corrections.why: The nomination says the concrete base and steel tower are essentially unchanged since construction (p. 9), so no second tower is recorded.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The USLHS place record gives 'Year Established: 1938', which is the year the Lighthouse Service announced its plan. The nomination and LighthouseFriends date the lighting to 1941. The facts block uses 1941.

The record gives the tower as 12.0 m. The nomination gives about 55 ft (16.8 m) from water to the top of the light tower and about 30 ft (9 m) for the steel tower alone. The facts block uses the nomination.
The nomination says visible for 11 miles in clear weather. Eleven statute miles is about 9.6 nautical miles, which matches the record.

notes_for_editor: No keeper roster: the USLHS place record lists none and says Keeper's Quarters: No. The nomination and LighthouseFriends say Coast Guard crews at Marquette Harbor Light maintained it by remote control until automation. The USLHS place record has two errors: Location 'Lake Huron' (the place is Marquette, Lake Superior) and 'Active Aid to Navigation? No' (the nomination says the light operates). The Lighthouse Service Bulletin 1912-1939 index and volumes mention 'Presque Isle, Mich.' only for the Lake Huron light near Alpena, and 'Presque Isle Pierhead' for Erie, Pennsylvania; none of those is this light, and they were not used. Chronicling America (Michigan papers, 1936-1965, 'Presque Isle Harbor' with 'breakwater') returned no hits. The 1988 drowning rests on the Carnegie Hero Fund record and a Mining Journal column reprinting a 1989 notice; the UPI 1988 report and an NMU PDF were blocked (403) and were not used. The two men are private individuals who died; the story names them only as those sources do. Wikipedia was read for leads only and is not cited. The brief's alias 'Gull Island' is unverified and was not used. The 1940 Lake Carriers' Association forecast is cited only as quoted by LighthouseFriends (copyrighted; facts and one short quotation). No photos were located.
